doc.title: Al Chez interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, February 13, 2019

title: Pageantry in his blood and teaching marching bands today
summary: Chez says drum corps pageantry is in his DNA and describes teaching DCI corps and running three high school band programs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well there’s a pageantry to that music obviously. And I wonder if you got that in your blood and now when you get on stage tonight that some of that pageantry and that entertainment factor goes into your band.

Oh without a doubt. It’s embedded in my DNA because I’ve been doing it for so long. I still do it. I go to San Antonio, Texas and I teach a DCI Drum & Bugle Corps from San Antonio, Texas. I teach one from Harrisburg, New Jersey. I run three high school band programs where I’m the coordinator, where I create the drill and I create the program and I pick the music that we’re going to play and I choreograph the whole thing. And I absolutely love it. I’m a marching band/DCI Drum Corps nerd.
